title: New grep guard for the reset-arm rt_landlord_id clear also matches the pre-existing consent-changed handler, so it cannot detect a regression
evidence: New guard token: document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null — this exact substring already appears verbatim in the unchanged consent-changed handler: window.posthog.opt_out_capturing();document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;
detail: The pinned substring pre-exists in the consent-rejection branch, so the guard passes even if the new reset-arm clear is deleted. It cannot catch the regression it was added to prevent.
recommended_fix: Pin a reset-arm-only adjacency, e.g. the rt_ph_reset clear immediately followed by the rt_landlord_id clear, which appears nowhere else in the snippet.

title: OAuth insert-vs-update detection relies on the undocumented PostgreSQL xmax MVCC field
detail: Using xmax to distinguish INSERT from UPDATE in ON CONFLICT is a known but undocumented PostgreSQL implementation detail, not a stable SQL contract. Reliable today; the integration test covers only the sequential case.
recommended_fix: Acceptable as-is since the test guards it, but note in the comment that xmax semantics are PG-internal and re-verify on any Postgres major-version upgrade.
